entries.summary: Four Pungs/Kongs and a pair, all made from Winds and Dragons.
entries.whatItIs: A normal grouped hand containing only honour tiles, with four Pungs or Kongs and one pair.
entries.whatItMeans: Every meld and the pair must be made from Winds or Dragons; suited tiles do not appear in the reviewed shared structure.
entries.whySpecial: The entire ordinary hand structure is restricted to the seven honour tile families.

entries.summary: Four Pungs/Kongs and a pair made only from suited 1s and 9s.
entries.whatItIs: A grouped hand made entirely from terminal suit tiles, with no Winds or Dragons.
entries.whatItMeans: Only the 1 and 9 of the three numbered suits can appear, and they must form the four melds and pair.
entries.whySpecial: The hand keeps an ordinary grouped shape while restricting every tile to suited terminals.

entries.summary: Four Kongs plus a pair.
entries.whatItIs: An ordinary grouped hand in which all four melds are Kongs.
entries.whatItMeans: Each of the four meld positions is a four-of-a-kind Kong; the pair completes the hand.
entries.whySpecial: Four Kongs expand the physical hand beyond fourteen tiles and occupy every meld position with the largest set type.

entries.summary: Pairs of Green and Red Dragons plus five Bamboo pairs.
entries.whatItIs: A seven-pair hand combining a Green Dragon pair, a Red Dragon pair and five Bamboo pairs.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand is organised entirely as pairs rather than normal melds, with the two coloured Dragon pairs fixed and the remaining five pairs in Bamboo.
entries.whySpecial: It combines a complete seven-pair structure with a tightly specified Dragon-and-Bamboo composition.

entries.summary: All four 1 Bamboo tiles plus pairs of 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 Bamboo.
entries.whatItIs: A fixed Bamboo-only irregular hand containing the complete four copies of 1 Bamboo and five specified pairs.
entries.whatItMeans: Unlike a normal grouped hand, qualification comes from matching a fixed fourteen-tile Bamboo collection.
entries.whySpecial: The composition is almost completely fixed: four copies of one rank and pairs of five named ranks.

entries.summary: One Chow in each suit, your own Wind as a Pung/Kong, and a Dragon pair.
entries.whatItIs: A grouped hand combining one Chow from each numbered suit with a Pung/Kong of the player's own Wind and a Dragon pair.
entries.whatItMeans: The player's seat Wind is part of the qualification, so the same tile layout may qualify for one player and not another.
entries.whySpecial: It deliberately combines all three suits with player-specific Wind context and a Dragon pair.

entries.summary: A four-tile consecutive run in each suit plus an honour pair; matching run starts form the higher treatment.
entries.whatItIs: A family of irregular three-suit hands built from one four-tile run in each suit and an honour pair.
entries.whatItMeans: The base form allows the three runs to start at different ranks. A separate higher treatment applies when all three four-tile runs match exactly.
entries.whySpecial: The hand uses three four-tile runs that are not ordinary Chows, and the relationship between their starting ranks changes the treatment.

variants.label: Big Robert
variants.definition: One consecutive four-tile run in each suit, with an honour pair; the run starts are not all the same.

variants.label: Big Robert — matching runs
variants.definition: Matching consecutive four-tile runs in all three suits, plus an honour pair.

entries.summary: One of each Wind plus five pairs in one numbered suit.
entries.whatItIs: An irregular hand made from all four Winds as single tiles and five same-suit pairs.
entries.whatItMeans: The Winds are not melds; they form four distinct single honours while the remaining ten tiles form five pairs in one suit.
entries.whySpecial: It combines four unpaired Wind identities with a five-pair single-suit structure rather than normal melds.

entries.summary: A Pung/Kong of 1s in each suit, plus all four Winds with one Wind paired.
entries.whatItIs: A hybrid hand combining terminal Pungs/Kongs in all three suits with all four Wind identities and a Wind pair.
entries.whatItMeans: The three suit groups are fixed to rank 1; the remaining five tiles are the four Winds with one duplicated to make the pair.
entries.whySpecial: It binds the same terminal rank across all three suits to a complete four-Wind collection.

entries.summary: A Pung/Kong of 9s in each suit, plus all four Winds with one Wind paired.
entries.whatItIs: A hybrid hand combining terminal Pungs/Kongs in all three suits with all four Wind identities and a Wind pair.
entries.whatItMeans: The three suit groups are fixed to rank 9; the remaining five tiles are the four Winds with one duplicated to make the pair.
entries.whySpecial: It binds the same terminal rank across all three suits to a complete four-Wind collection.

entries.summary: One Chow in each suit, plus all four Winds with one Wind paired.
entries.whatItIs: A hybrid special combining three suited Chows with a complete set of four distinct Winds and one Wind duplicate.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand contains one Chow from every suit; the five remaining tiles are all four Winds with one forming the pair.
entries.whySpecial: It combines all three suits and all four Winds in one fixed mixed structure.

entries.summary: A one-suit 1-8 or 2-9 run plus three Wind or Dragon pairs.
entries.whatItIs: An irregular hand containing eight consecutive suited tiles and three honour pairs from one honour family.
entries.whatItMeans: The suited section is a single-tile run rather than Chows; the other six tiles form three pairs of Winds or three pairs of Dragons.
entries.whySpecial: It joins an eight-tile straight with a three-pair honour block, producing a complete non-standard fourteen-tile structure.

entries.summary: One single of each Dragon, a Pung/Kong in each suit, and a suited pair.
entries.whatItIs: A special hand combining three ungrouped Dragon singles with one suited Pung/Kong from each suit and a suited pair.
entries.whatItMeans: The Dragons deliberately remain single; the grouped part of the hand is spread across all three suits.
entries.whySpecial: It uses all three Dragons without forming Dragon sets, alongside one meld from every numbered suit.

entries.summary: All three Dragons with one Dragon paired, plus five pairs in one suit.
entries.whatItIs: An irregular pair-based hand containing the three Dragon identities, one of them as a pair, and five suited pairs from one suit.
entries.whatItMeans: Four Dragon tiles occupy the honour portion; the other ten tiles form five pairs within a single numbered suit.
entries.whySpecial: It combines the complete Dragon family with a five-pair single-suit block instead of normal melds.

entries.summary: A complete 1-9 run in one suit, one of each Dragon, plus a pair of one Dragon.
entries.whatItIs: An irregular hand joining a nine-tile suited straight to all three Dragon identities with one Dragon additionally paired.
entries.whatItMeans: The 1-9 suited run uses nine singles; the remaining five tiles are one of each Dragon plus an extra two copies of one Dragon to form the pair alongside its single.
entries.whySpecial: The hand combines a complete one-suit straight with a complete Dragon-family pattern rather than ordinary melds.

entries.summary: A Green Dragon Pung with Bamboo Pungs/Kongs and a Bamboo pair.
entries.whatItIs: A grouped hand centred on a Green Dragon Pung and otherwise entirely Bamboo Pungs/Kongs plus a Bamboo pair.
entries.whatItMeans: Green Dragon is the only honour component; every suited group and the pair come from Bamboo.
entries.whySpecial: It links a specific Dragon colour to a single suited family while retaining a normal grouped hand shape.

entries.summary: A Red Dragon Pung with Character Pungs/Kongs and a Character pair.
entries.whatItIs: A grouped hand centred on a Red Dragon Pung and otherwise entirely Character Pungs/Kongs plus a Character pair.
entries.whatItMeans: Red Dragon is the only honour component; every suited group and the pair come from Characters.
entries.whySpecial: It links a specific Dragon to a single suited family while retaining a normal grouped hand shape.

entries.summary: A White Dragon Pung with Circle Pungs/Kongs and a Circle pair.
entries.whatItIs: A grouped hand centred on a White Dragon Pung and otherwise entirely Circle Pungs/Kongs plus a Circle pair.
entries.whatItMeans: White Dragon is the only honour component; every suited group and the pair come from Circles.
entries.whySpecial: It links a specific Dragon to a single suited family while retaining a normal grouped hand shape.

entries.summary: A complete 1-9 run as three Chows, plus a same-suit Pung and pair.
entries.whatItIs: A one-suit grouped hand containing the three Chows 1-2-3, 4-5-6 and 7-8-9, plus a Pung and pair in that same suit.
entries.whatItMeans: The three Chows guarantee every rank 1 through 9 appears; the final Pung and pair repeat ranks from that same suit within physical copy limits.
entries.whySpecial: It combines the complete suited sequence with both a triplet and pair while staying entirely in one suit.

entries.summary: A complete 1-9 run plus an honour Pung/Kong; Western permits any pair, while Outside the Box requires a suited pair.
entries.whatItIs: A family of grouped hands built from a 1-9 suited run and an honour Pung/Kong, with rules-specific pair qualification.
entries.whatItMeans: The three-Chow run and honour meld are shared. The important difference is the pair: Thompson & Maloney allows any pair; Outside the Box narrows this to a suited pair.
entries.whySpecial: A single pair restriction changes the set of qualifying hands even though the visible run-and-honour core is the same.

variants.label: Western — any pair
variants.definition: A 1-9 run, an honour Pung/Kong and any pair.

variants.label: Outside the Box — suited pair
variants.definition: A 1-9 run, an honour Pung/Kong and a suited pair.
